issues.description: Field ExcellenceLand.excellencyLevel: the UML in the problem statement declares the attribute as type double, but the reference implementation in solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/ExcellenceLand.java declares it as int. This mismatch affects the constructor parameter type and the getter return type, and will confuse students which type to implement to follow the UML and constructor signature requirements.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of ExcellenceLand.excellencyLevel consistent across the exercise. Either: (A) Update the solution and template Java files so the field, the constructor parameter, and the getter use double (change the declaration in src/de/tum/in/ase/ExcellenceLand.java to 'private double excellencyLevel;', update the constructor parameter and assignment, and change getExcellencyLevel() to return double), or (B) Update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare excellencyLevel as int. Choose the option that reflects the intended precision (double if fractional values are expected, int if only integers are intended) and apply the change consistently in the template, solution, and problem statement.
